note: Public signals only. They describe the city, not whether a given organization has local support. Statuses (POSITIVE / NEUTRAL / NEGATIVE / UNKNOWN) are FourFold's reading of each source, labelled ASSUMPTION where they are a judgment.

signals.label: Housing element compliance (6th cycle)
signals.value: In compliance. HCD received the adopted element 2022-07-26 and reviewed it 2022-09-16 (status: In).
signals.meaning: The city has a housing element HCD finds in compliance, so its housing plan is in place and a nonprofit can point to the city's own housing goals when it asks for support.

source.name: HCD Housing Element Compliance Report (data.ca.gov), resource 2dcd1cd4-1348-4fc5-9c9c-219f82daac00, dataset updated 2026-11-06

signals.label: 6th cycle RHNA progress (2021-10-15 to 2029-10-15)
signals.value: Very low income 359 of 606 (59%). Low income 426 of 362 (118%). Moderate 260 of 545 (48%). Above moderate 2,978 of 1,624 (183%).
signals.meaning: The city is ahead on market-rate and low-income homes but behind on very low and moderate income homes. Affordable ownership homes from a nonprofit would count toward the categories where the city is behind, which is a reason to bring the project to the housing division early. ASSUMPTION: FourFold treats this as neutral, not as support.

source.name: HCD RHNA Progress Report, 6th Cycle (data.ca.gov), resource 1e80a9cf-724c-432d-8374-e9708a6a92dc. HCD's data dictionary describes the unit fields as units completed during the planning period, summed from APR Table A2.

signals.label: SB 9 projects the city reports to HCD
signals.value: UNKNOWN. Santa Ana files APR building activity every year 2022 to 2025, but no row is labelled SB 9.
signals.meaning: We cannot tell from state data whether the city has approved SB 9 lot splits. Ask the housing division or planning how many it has processed.

source.name: HCD APR Tables A and A2 (data.ca.gov), as summarized in FourFold data/comparables.json

signals.label: HCD Housing Accountability Unit letters to the city
signals.value: UNKNOWN. The HCD letters dashboard is an embedded app we could not read without browser automation. A web search points to a 2023 HCD technical assistance letter in city records about proposed AB 2011 parcel exemptions, but the city records portal would not open for us, so it is a lead, not a confirmed fact.
signals.meaning: An enforcement letter about SB 9 or ADUs would warn that the city has pushed back on small-lot housing. We did not confirm any. Check the dashboard by jurisdiction before making an offer.

source.name: HCD Technical Assistance and Enforcement Letters Dashboard

signals.label: City SB 9 ordinance or handout
signals.value: UNKNOWN. A web search points to a Santa Ana urgency ordinance (NS-3013) on urban lot splits and two-unit projects in city records, but the records portal would not open for us. We did not find an SB 9 page on santa-ana.gov.
signals.meaning: Local SB 9 rules decide how easy a lot split will be. Ask planning for the current SB 9 rules and any handout before an offer.

source.name: Santa Ana city council records (Laserfiche WebLink), lead only

signals.label: City pre-approved ADU plans program
signals.value: Yes. The city publishes a Pre-Approved ADU Plans page with plan downloads.
signals.meaning: The city already runs a program to speed up small-scale homes. This is about ADUs, not SB 9, so it is a weak signal about lot splits. ASSUMPTION: FourFold counts it as a mild positive.

source.name: City of Santa Ana, Pre-Approved ADU Plans
